content:
droid-monkey attacked this Android app with a real-world fault and it failed. Fix the root cause.

## What happened
Attack `process_death` (process_death): Fill the screen's form, let Android kill the app in the background, then come back to it.
Steps: [{"fill": true}, {"fault": "kill_in_background"}, {"fault": "relaunch"}, {"settle": 6}]
Result: lost_state: 6 of 6 filled fields changed or emptied
Fields lost (before -> after): {'field_name': ['Ravi Kumar', ''], 'field_email': ['ravi@example.com', ''], 'field_phone': ['9876543210', ''], 'field_address': ['12 MG Road', ''], 'field_city': ['Bengaluru', ''], 'field_pincode': ['560001', '']}

## Diagnosis
Root cause: The checkout form's six fields are plain `mutableStateOf` properties on `CheckoutViewModel` (CheckoutViewModel.kt:14-19), and the ViewModel is obtained via the default `viewModel()` factory with no SavedStateHandle (CheckoutScreen.kt:34). A ViewModel survives only configuration changes, not process death, so when Android kills the backgrounded app the VM and all typed input are discarded. MainActivity does persist the route with `rememberSaveable` (MainActivity.kt:62), so the user lands back on the checkout screen, but it is a freshly constructed ViewModel with every field blank, which is exactly the observed loss (all six fields emptied). The form's state was never put anywhere that survives process death.
Fix approach: Make the form state survive process death by backing each field with SavedStateHandle (e.g. `private val saved: SavedStateHandle` with `saved.getStateFlow("name", "")` or a `saved["name"]` setter-backed property) so the values are written to the saved-state bundle. Inject it via the default ViewModel factory (`viewModel()` provides SavedStateHandle automatically when the ViewModel constructor takes it), so no extra factory is needed. Alternatively use `rememberSaveable` for each field in CheckoutScreen, but the ViewModel-with-SavedStateHandle route keeps the fields in one place alongside placeOrder.
Evidence: app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CheckoutViewModel.kt:13-19 - ViewModel has no SavedStateHandle; six form fields are plain mutableStateOf, lost when the process is killed; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CheckoutViewModel.kt:27 - isComplete depends only on those in-memory fields, so it is false after restore and Place order stays disabled; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CheckoutScreen.kt:34 - vm = viewModel() uses the default factory with no saved-state handle wiring; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CheckoutScreen.kt:67-72 - each CheckoutField reads and writes the VM's in-memory property directly, with no rememberSaveable backing; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/MainActivity.kt:62 - route is persisted with rememberSaveable, so the screen is restored while the form data is not, which produces the blank-form symptom; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/MainActivity.kt:80 - CheckoutScreen(route.productId) is hosted without any form state being passed in or saved

## Files to change
- app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CheckoutViewModel.kt
- app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CheckoutScreen.kt

## Regression test
Add a JVM unit test `CheckoutViewModelProcessDeathTest` in src/test: create `CheckoutViewModel(SavedStateHandle())`, set name='Ravi Kumar', email, phone, address, city, pincode, then build a second ViewModel from a SavedStateHandle restored from the first one's saved state (e.g. `SavedStateHandle(mapOf(...))` copied from the first handle's `savedStateProvider().saveState()` or simply reuse the handle's values) and assert every field equals the original and `isComplete` is true. Before the fix the constructor takes no SavedStateHandle, so the test fails to compile/returns blank values; after the fix it passes.

## Rules
- Fix the root cause in the files above with the idiomatic Android approach. Keep the change small and focused.
- Add exactly one regression test file under app/src/test (JVM unit test, preferred) or app/src/androidTest
  (instrumented), using only test libraries the project already has (see app/build.gradle.kts). It must fail on
  the old code and pass on the fixed code.
- Do not change build files or add dependencies. Do not touch unrelated code. Do not commit.
- When done, reply with one short paragraph: what you changed and the test class name.

- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".

- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

package com.shubhasai.monkeymart.ui

import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Arrangement
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.fillMaxSize
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.fillMaxWidth
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.padding
import androidx.compose.foundation.rememberScrollState
import androidx.compose.foundation.text.KeyboardOptions
import androidx.compose.foundation.verticalScroll
import androidx.compose.material3.Button
import androidx.compose.material3.Card
import androidx.compose.material3.CircularProgressIndicator
import androidx.compose.material3.MaterialTheme
import androidx.compose.material3.OutlinedTextField
import androidx.compose.material3.Text
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.ui.platform.LocalContext
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import androidx.compose.ui.platform.testTag
import androidx.compose.ui.text.input.KeyboardType
import androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp
import androidx.lifecycle.viewmodel.compose.viewModel
import com.shubhasai.monkeymart.data.OrderRepository
import com.shubhasai.monkeymart.data.ProductRepository
import com.shubhasai.monkeymart.data.priceLabel

@Composable
fun CheckoutScreen(
    productId: Int,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    vm: CheckoutViewModel = viewModel(),
) {
    val product = ProductRepository.cached(productId)
    val context = LocalContext.current
    val orders = remember { OrderRepository(context) }

    val placedId = vm.orderId
    if (placedId != null) {
        Column(modifier.fillMaxSize().padding(24.dp).testTag("order_confirmed"), verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(8.dp)) {
            Text("Order placed 🎉", style = MaterialTheme.typography.headlineSmall)
            Text("Order $placedId is on its way to ${vm.city}.", modifier = Modifier.testTag("order_id"))
        }
        return
    }

    Column(
        modifier = modifier
            .fillMaxSize()
            .verticalScroll(rememberScrollState())
            .padding(16.dp)
            .testTag("checkout_screen"),
        verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(8.dp),
    ) {
        if (product != null) {
            Card(Modifier.fillMaxWidth()) {
                Row(Modifier.padding(16.dp), horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.SpaceBetween) {
                    Text("${product.emoji} ${product.name}", style = MaterialTheme.typography.titleMedium, modifier = Modifier.weight(1f))
                    Text(product.priceLabel(), style = MaterialTheme.typography.titleMedium, modifier = Modifier.testTag("checkout_total"))
                }
            }
        }

        Text("Delivery details", style = MaterialTheme.typography.titleMedium)
        CheckoutField("Full name", vm.name, { vm.name = it }, "field_name")
        CheckoutField("Email", vm.email, { vm.email = it }, "field_email", KeyboardType.Email)
        CheckoutField("Phone", vm.phone, { vm.phone = it }, "field_phone", KeyboardType.Phone)
        CheckoutField("Address", vm.address, { vm.address = it }, "field_address")
        CheckoutField("City", vm.city, { vm.city = it }, "field_city")
        CheckoutField("Pincode", vm.pincode, { vm.pincode = it }, "field_pincode", KeyboardType.Number)

        ScanCouponButton()

        Button(
            onClick = { vm.placeOrder(orders, productId) },
            enabled = vm.isComplete && !vm.placing,
            modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth().testTag("place_order"),
        ) {
            if (vm.placing) CircularProgressIndicator(Modifier.testTag("placing_order")) else Text("Place order")
        }
    }
}

@Composable
private fun CheckoutField(
    label: String,
    value: String,
    onChange: (String) -> Unit,
    tag: String,
    keyboard: KeyboardType = KeyboardType.Text,
) {
    OutlinedTextField(
        value = value,
        onValueChange = onChange,
        label = { Text(label) },
        singleLine = true,
        keyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions(keyboardType = keyboard),
        modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth().testTag(tag),
    )
}

I made the checkout form survive process death by having `CheckoutViewModel` take a `SavedStateHandle` and back all six fields with it. I haven't run the build or the test.

Each field is still Compose-observable state, but every write is also saved to the handle. A new ViewModel reads its starting values from the handle, so the form comes back filled after Android kills the app. `CheckoutScreen.kt` needed no change, because the default `viewModel()` factory already supplies the `SavedStateHandle`.

The regression test is `CheckoutViewModelProcessDeathTest`, in `app/src/test/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/`. It fills all six fields, builds a second ViewModel from a new handle seeded with the first handle's values, and asserts every field matches and `isComplete` is true. I seeded it with a map instead of calling `saveState()` because that returns an Android `Bundle`, which isn't available in a JVM unit test. It fails on the old code because the constructor takes no handle.
